tagline: A UNESCO seascape of 1,600 limestone islands — explored today on ~500 diesel junk boats. The water is the destination; it should also be the clean way through it.
summary: Ha Long Bay and the adjoining Lan Ha / Cat Ba archipelago are Vietnam's marquee marine destination, inside a province that drew ~19 million visitors in 2024. The entire experience happens on the water — yet it runs on roughly 500 registered diesel tourist boats whose emissions and discharge UNESCO and Quang Ninh authorities have repeatedly flagged in a protected World Heritage bay. This is the rare destination where clean, silent, near-wake-free marine mobility isn't a nice-to-have — it's the conservation mandate and the premium experience at once.

demand_signals.label: Province visitor volume
demand_signals.note: Quang Ninh hit its 19M target; Ha Long City alone took 9.2M in the first nine months (+33% YoY) — almost all of it funnels onto the bay.

demand_signals.label: The diesel-junk-boat fleet
demand_signals.note: Every visit to the bay is a boat trip; the fleet is overwhelmingly diesel and is the headline pressure on a UNESCO site.

demand_signals.label: Protected-bay water quality under pressure
demand_signals.note: The Ha Long–Cat Ba World Heritage report cites continued discharge from boats; conservation initiatives are already limiting cruise-boat numbers.

demand_signals.label: International cruise & superyacht arrivals
demand_signals.note: Ha Long International Cruise Port and a growing superyacht segment need premium last-mile-on-water transfers into the islands.

use_cases.title: Clean, silent island-cruising in a World Heritage bay
use_cases.body: Replace diesel day-boats with all-electric foiling between Tuan Chau, the central karst islands, Bai Tu Long and Lan Ha Bay. Near-silent, near-wake-free, zero in-bay emissions — the exact profile UNESCO and Quang Ninh want, sold to visitors as the smoothest, fastest way to see the bay.

use_cases.title: Cruise-port & superyacht premium transfers
use_cases.body: Foiling transfers from Ha Long International Cruise Port and visiting superyachts directly to island anchorages and Lan Ha coves — a refined alternative to chartered diesel tenders for the high-spend segment.

use_cases.title: Cat Ba / Hai Phong gateway shuttle
use_cases.body: A high-frequency clean shuttle linking Tuan Chau, Cat Ba Island and the Hai Phong mainland (Cat Bi airport gateway), turning a slow ferry-and-road hop into a direct foiling crossing.

journeys.to: Lan Ha Bay / Cat Ba Island
journeys.today: A slow diesel junk-boat cruise or a ferry-plus-road combination; engine noise, fumes and wake inside a protected bay.
journeys.with_navier: A direct all-electric foiling hop — silent, smooth and zero-emission across the karst seascape, arriving fresh at the Lan Ha anchorages.

journeys.today: Transfer to a chartered diesel tender; limited range and a heavy footprint in quieter, less-visited waters.
journeys.with_navier: A clean foiling tour into the less-crowded Bai Tu Long islands — opening premium itineraries without adding diesel load to the heritage zone.

journeys.today: Ferry plus road, or the new expressway loop — fine for cars, slow and indirect for people heading to/from the airport.
journeys.with_navier: A direct foiling shuttle across the channel; Quanta-LR can extend the same clean corridor down the Gulf of Tonkin coast when the network grows.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Ideal: every meaningful leg in and around the bay — Tuan Chau↔Cat Ba/Lan Ha (~12 nm), cruise-port↔Bai Tu Long (~9 nm), Ha Long↔Hai Phong (~16 nm) — sits well inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope, and zero in-bay emissions is the literal conservation requirement of a UNESCO site.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Extends the clean corridor beyond the bay along the Gulf of Tonkin coast (toward Hai Phong city, Do Son, outer Bai Tu Long and future coastal nodes) and removes any charging-infrastructure dependency for remote island anchorages where shore power is thin.

competitive_landscape: Today the bay is run almost entirely by conventional diesel tour-boat and cruise operators — roughly 500 registered vessels, from day-trip junks to overnight cruisers (Bhaya, Paradise, Indochina and many more) — plus Tuan Chau↔Cat Ba car ferries. The volume proves the demand; the diesel footprint, noise and wake inside a World Heritage seascape are exactly the status quo Navier improves on. Operators already run voluntary 'Clean The Bay' clean-ups, signalling an industry that knows it has an environmental problem to solve.

precedents.what: Industry-led 'Clean The Bay' programs and active conservation limits on cruise-boat numbers
precedents.why_it_matters: The operators and the province already accept that the diesel fleet is the problem — a clean-marine network is a solution they are primed to adopt, not a concept to be sold from scratch.

seasonality: Peak season is the cool, dry months (Oct–Apr); summer (May–Sep) brings heat, occasional typhoons and the NE-monsoon shoulder when chop and fog force junk-boat cancellations and rough rides. Foiling's stability and higher cruise speed mean a smoother, more reliable ride and the ability to recover schedule on marginal-sea-state days when conventional boats are delayed — while the protected, island-sheltered water keeps most legs benign year-round.
regulatory_note: Quang Ninh provincial authorities and the Ha Long Bay Management Board regulate vessel access to a UNESCO World Heritage Site (jointly inscribed with the Cat Ba Archipelago, 2023) under active water-quality and emissions scrutiny. A zero-emission, low-wake fleet aligns directly with conservation mandates and Vietnam's national net-zero-by-2050 commitment, making clean-fleet certification a tailwind rather than a hurdle.
